feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/operations leadership. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and dense, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization support trust and show increasing responsibility.  
- Good impact signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and analytics stack details add substance.  
- Strong positioning for digital strategy roles: combines communications leadership, CMS/platform expertise, analytics, and multimedia production.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten repetition and structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to save space and improve focus.  
- Add more outcome-based results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than measurable business/communications outcomes (growth, engagement, efficiency, revenue, campaign performance).  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without final comma); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, one or two concrete differentiators, and less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with your current value proposition: senior digital strategy/communications leader for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a sharper summary of outcomes: cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, governance, and content operations.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, content operations, editorial workflows, and digital governance across web, email, social, and multimedia channels. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, accessible messaging and aligning stakeholders around effective advocacy communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder coordination” also appears elsewhere; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized higher-value, differentiating capabilities and used parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize wording: use plural or noun-phrase format consistently.
- Replace broad items like “Multi-channel communication” with more specific, senior-level language.
- Prioritize strengths most supported by recent roles: platform modernization, CMS governance, analytics, and cross-functional leadership.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS governance • Editorial operations & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Systems architecture & process improvement • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy, advocacy & member communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Policy & advocacy communication” and “Multi-channel communication” are already strongly covered in the header and Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current item with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and 2–3 signature contributions so it feels distinct from the NACo roles below.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership language: “Built,” “Led,” “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Established.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; e.g. combine digital systems/workflows/analytics + governance/operations into one bullet on enterprise communications infrastructure.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages, users, teams supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing speed, search success, engagement, or efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” overlaps with the Recent Projects section; keep one concise mention here and let the project entry carry detail.
- Drupal/CMS/front-end work may repeat skills sections; focus this item on business impact, not tool lists.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, budget, and multi-channel communications across web, email, social, and video.”
- Combine scale + transformation: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add metrics for email/social growth, video output, production savings, reporting speed, stakeholder adoption, or governance efficiency.
- Tighten weaker bullets: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels…” with a result-focused line on audience growth, engagement, or campaign performance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/social/video operations overlap with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, and systems.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; mention the studio here, save recurring series specifics for projects/earlier roles.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item currently reads as a lighter version of the more senior NACo role above and overlaps with the earlier NACo role below. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational ownership, cross-team coordination, and channel growth with sharper outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite opening to stress scope and ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and measurable if possible: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, cadence, or audience growth if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems statement: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier NACo role and footer project; differentiate by focusing here on scaling/operationalizing it.
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” overlaps with the Director role; avoid repeating broad channel oversight language.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive strengths rather than broad, generic phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content strategy” to sound more senior and aligned with director/consultant-level work.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this skills block to scale from recent roles (e.g., 10,000+ page Drupal migration, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views) rather than trying to imply impact here.
- Keep terminology consistent with recent roles: use “governance,” “editorial operations,” and “cross-channel” to mirror the strongest experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat language already used in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it currently reads like a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent work, not repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal & enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older/less-evidenced items here, especially “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” “Power Pages,” and “jQuery,” unless they are central to target roles.
- Use “front-end implementation” instead of listing too many languages; it reads more senior and aligns with recent Drupal/platform work.
- If you want one sharper version: “Drupal & enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization • Front-end implementation • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills broader and save full tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies/header language; keep wording consistent, not repetitive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g.: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI) • User behavior insights (Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO and performance optimization”
- Consider grouping tools in parentheses to reduce listiness and improve scanability.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows, add one impact-oriented qualifier tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web modernization” or “decision-ready reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- “SEO and performance analysis” overlaps with the Technical + IT line item “SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing production environment and delivery scope rather than broad video terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Studio, Livestream & Hybrid Event Production**
- Tighten content to: **Livestream and hybrid event production • Broadcast-style studio operations • PTZ camera systems and switching • Video production/editing**
- If accurate, add scale/context instead of generic terms: **Multi-camera livestream delivery**, **virtual event production**, or **in-house studio buildout and operation**
- Keep to 4 bullets max and order by strongest differentiators: hybrid/livestream, studio ops, PTZ/switching, editing

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is already supported by multiple work-experience bullets; avoid over-weighting it here.
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies; use more specific phrasing like **multi-camera livestream delivery** or **broadcast-style studio operations**.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform in the experience, this item should emphasize depth/order rather than read as a generic list.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency framing: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider tightening to the platforms you’ve used most substantively in recent roles; if GitHub Pages was minor, remove it.
- If you want more impact, rename the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** and align it with your modernization/governance positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry; keep one as a short platform list and let the other carry broader technical capabilities.
- Drupal already appears prominently in recent experience, so avoid overloading multiple sections with the same undifferentiated list.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as applied capabilities, e.g.: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group tools by function for clarity: “Integrations & tagging: API integrations, Google Tag Manager”
- Keep newer/more distinctive tools prominent: “Edge/serverless & deployment: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider concise rewrite: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tagging integrations (Google Tag Manager) • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in Topline Skills; keep it in one place or shorten one version.
- “API integrations” and broader technical execution also overlap with Core Competencies and recent freelance bullets; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from app list to capability-led grouping: “Workflow automation & collaboration: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team operations: Slack, Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira/Asana. Consider dropping weaker/common tools like Slack and Teams if space is tight.
- If accurate, add a qualifier showing depth: “built automations,” “managed editorial workflows,” or “cross-team planning systems” to connect tools to outcomes.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; “Automation & Workflow Systems” could become “Workflow Automation & Team Operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are generic collaboration tools and may dilute the stronger systems/automation signal.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of capability. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize enterprise-level systems rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten the list to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- If one platform was primary, order by strongest/recentest use rather than alphabetically

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email” is already covered in multiple recent work bullets; avoid adding phrases like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy” here
- “Engagement” may overlap with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; keep this item tool-focused rather than broad capability-focused

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, platform refresh support, and hands-on production.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer action/result language: “Supported a major website refresh, improving publishing coordination and day-to-day digital operations.”
- Tighten production phrasing: “Produced recurring livestreams and weekly video content that expanded NACo’s in-house multimedia output.”
- Make supervision concise: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.” If possible, add metrics (content volume, audience growth, event count, or production cadence).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version framed as launching/building the format, not scaling it.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes so it complements—rather than repeats—your later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, recording coordination, and production.”
- Tighten the rest into one impact-oriented clause: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy communications.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer function: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program visibility and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audiences served, project outputs, or programs/policy teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content/multimedia” language that overlaps with the stronger 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize team leadership here; later roles already establish progression into management.
